```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center", out.width = "100%")
source("../../_shared/template/viscount_rmd_helpers.R")
library(jsonlite)

read_json_file <- function (arg0_path) {
  txt <- readLines(arg0_path, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
  fromJSON(paste(txt, collapse = "\n"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
}

mod_data <- read_json_file("western_amazon_basin.json5")
set_data <- read_json_file("western_amazon_basin_settlements.json")
led_data <- read_json_file("western_amazon_basin_source_ledger.json5")

clean_text <- function (arg0_s) {
  s <- gsub("&", "and", as.character(arg0_s), fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("_", " ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("%", "\\\\%", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("#", "\\\\#", s, fixed = TRUE)
  trimws(s)
}

fmt_yr <- function (arg0_y) {
  y <- as.numeric(arg0_y)
  if (y < 0) return(paste0(abs(round(y)), "BC"))
  return(paste0(round(y), "AD"))
}

fmt_coord <- function (arg0_coords) {
  lat <- as.numeric(arg0_coords[[1]])
  lon <- as.numeric(arg0_coords[[2]])
  lat_s <- paste0(viscount_fmt_number(abs(lat), 2L), if (lat >= 0) " N" else " S")
  lon_s <- paste0(viscount_fmt_number(abs(lon), 2L), if (lon >= 0) " E" else " W")
  paste0(lat_s, ", ", lon_s)
}

set_list <- unname(set_data)
sett_peaks <- vapply(set_list, function (s) {
  if (is.null(s$population) || length(s$population) == 0) return(0)
  max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population)))
}, numeric(1))

reg_short <- list(
  wamz_central_amazon_rio_negro = "Central Amazon & Negro",
  wamz_madeira_guapore = "Madeira-Guaporé",
  wamz_llanos_de_moxos = "Llanos de Moxos",
  wamz_purus_jurua_acre = "Purus-Juruá-Acre",
  wamz_caqueta_putumayo_napo = "Solimões-Caquetá-Napo",
  wamz_maranon_ucayali = "Lower Marañón-Ucayali",
  wamz_peruvian_andean_sierra = "Peruvian-Ecuadorian Sierra"
)

exc_list <- Filter(function (c) identical(c$status, "excluded") || identical(c$included, FALSE), led_data$candidates)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer catalogues geographic coordinates, cultural affiliations, occupation spans and demographic trajectories for 3.325 pre-Columbian settlements across the Western Amazon Basin and its Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean headwaters (4,19M km², encompassing 4.186.006 km²) from 10000BC to 1542AD. Spanning seven organic HydroBASINS hydrological divisions, the gazetteer integrates the monumental imperial metropolises, terraced provincial *llactas* and *Qhapaq Ñan* settlements of the Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean Sierra (2.172 sites) alongside the lowland agro-urban traditions of Lower Marañón-Huallaga-Ucayali (399 sites), Llanos de Moxos (218 sites), Madeira-Guaporé (175 sites), Solimões-Caquetá-Putumayo-Napo (167 sites), Central Amazon-Rio Negro (109 sites) and Purus-Juruá-Acre (85 sites), while Bolivian Altiplano and Eastern Cordillera valleys are documented separately in the dedicated Bolivian Highlands gazetteer.

Catalogued settlement peaks span from early Holocene rockshelters to imperial highland metropolises led by Cusco (59,4k peak), Wari in Ayacucho (39,5k), Tomebamba-Cuenca (25,0k), Cajamarca (17,8k), Hatun Xauxa in the Mantaro Valley (15,8k), Huánuco Pampa (13,9k), Pikillacta (11,9k), Vilcashuamán (11,9k), Tunanmarca (10,9k) and Marcahuamachuco (10,9k), alongside major lowland and montane-rim complexes led by Sangay (9,5k), Cotoca in Llanos de Moxos (8,4k), Kilamope (6,5k), Landívar (5,1k), Kuélap (4,5k) and Manaus (4,5k). Every catalogued locality reconciles against 10.695 audited source-ledger candidates incorporating official Peru Ministry of Culture SIGDA pre-Hispanic monuments (28.338 raw records), Colombia ICANH sites (22.146 raw records), p3k14c/AndesC14 radiocarbon contexts, Brazil IPHAN SICG and published Andean-Amazonian monographs, with 7.370 documented spatial deduplications within 3 km and zero unaccounted records.

By coupling georeferenced imperial highland capitals, provincial Andean monuments and lowland Terra Preta and earthwork settlements across a single hydrologically nested watershed, this gazetteer establishes an exhaustive empirical baseline for pre-contact nucleation across the entire Western Amazon and Central Andean eastern drainage.

# Settlement Archaeology across the Andean-Amazonian Watershed

Archaeological settlement patterns across the Western Amazon Basin and its Andean headwaters reflect six primary regional traditions [@neves2003historical; @prumers2022casarabe; @rostain2024upano; @bauer2004ancient; @isbell1991huari; @daltroy2015incas]:

1. **Central Andean Imperial Capitals and Terraced Valley Polities**: Across the Amazon-draining basins of the Upper Marañón, Mantaro, Apurímac, Vilcanota-Urubamba, Beni and Río Grande, Formative ceremonial centres (Chavín de Huántar, Kotosh, Kuntur Wasi), Middle Horizon Wari and Tiwanaku administrative hubs (Wari, Pikillacta, Cochabamba), Late Intermediate regional citadels (Kuélap, Tunanmarca, Marcahuamachuco, Iskanwaya) and Inca *Tawantinsuyu* planned metropolises (Cusco, Hatun Xauxa, Huánuco Pampa, Vilcashuamán, Incallajta, Tomebamba) anchored dense terraced agricultural landscapes documented across Peru SIGDA and Bolivian surveys [@sigda2024peru; @cook1981demographic; @capriles2023bolivian; @stanish2003ancient].
2. **Casarabe Monumental Urbanism**: In the seasonal savanna wetlands of Llanos de Moxos, Bolivia, the Casarabe culture constructed a hierarchical settlement system centred on stepped earthen pyramids rising up to twenty-one metres above monumental rectangular platforms [@prumers2022casarabe]. Primary centres at Cotoca and Landívar were connected to secondary mound centres and raised agricultural field belts by straight causeways and navigable canals spanning dozens of kilometres [@prumers2022casarabe; @walker2004agricultural].
3. **Upano Valley Garden Cities**: Along the eastern Andean foothills of Ecuador, the Kilamope and Upano cultures constructed thousands of monumental rectangular earthen platforms arranged in formal spatial complexes [@rostain2024upano]. Linked by wide sunken streets and integrated with drained agricultural plots, major centres at Sangay and Kilamope formed an interconnected agro-urban landscape flourishing from 500BC to 600AD [@rostain2024upano].
4. **Central Amazon Bluff Towns**: Along the high bluffs overlooking the Rio Negro and Solimões confluence, permanent settlements developed on deep anthropogenic dark earths (Terra Preta do Índio) [@neves2003historical; @lima2002ceramica]. Sites like Manaus, Açutuba, Hatahara and Manacapuru supported thousands of residents, protected by landward defensive ditches and palisades [@neves2014acutuba; @macedo2017pedogenetic].
5. **Acre Geometric Enclosures**: In the forested plateaus of Acre and northern Rondônia, indigenous builders excavated hundreds of circular, square and octagonal ditch-and-bank geoglyphs [@parssinen2009geoglyphs; @schaan2012sacred; @watling2017impact]. These monumental enclosures functioned as ceremonial assembly centres and defensive meeting grounds surrounded by managed palm orchards [@carson2014environmental; @desouza2018earthbuilders].
6. **Várzea Levee Settlements**: Along the white-water floodplains of the Solimões, Marañón and Ucayali, linear village settlements occupied natural river levees continuously for multiple kilometres [@lathrap1970upper; @myers1990sarabandero]. Supported by fertile annual silt deposition and aquatic harvesting, these chiefdoms maintained large fleets of war canoes and turtle corrals [@lathrap1970upper].

# Methodology and Source Ledger Reconciliation

Candidate sites in the source ledger were evaluated from official national archaeological heritage registries — Peru Ministry of Culture SIGDA (28.338 delimited, registered, declared and Qhapaq Ñan records), Colombia ICANH (22.146 official sites), Brazil IPHAN SICG (32.933 official sites), PEOPLE 3000 p3k14c/AndesC14 (6.264 South American radiocarbon dates), the Bolivian Radiocarbon Database and Wikidata georeferenced Andean monuments — alongside airborne LiDAR earthwork surveys and published excavation monographs [@sigda2024peru; @icanh2024colombia; @bird2022p3k14c; @capriles2023bolivian; @neves2003historical; @prumers2022casarabe; @rostain2024upano; @peripato2023earthworks]. Inclusion requires:
- Precise WGS84 geographic coordinates validated against HydroBASINS Level 5 and Level 6 catchments.
- Documented cultural horizons, official monument classifications or radiocarbon chronologies.
- Area-based or architectural-class demographic estimations calibrated to monument scale.

Where multiple archaeological survey points or monument sectors fall within 3 km of a primary nucleated settlement, secondary coordinates are consolidated as duplicate aliases, preserving geographic integrity and preventing artificial clustering.

Table \ref{tab:summary} summarises the distribution of 3.325 catalogued settlements and summed site peaks across all seven hydrological divisions.

```{r tbl-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(names(mod_data$regions), function (rk) {
  sub_sets <- Filter(function (s) identical(s$region_id, rk) || identical(s$region, rk), set_list)
  peaks <- if (length(sub_sets) > 0) vapply(sub_sets, function (s) max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population))), numeric(1)) else 0
  top_name <- if (length(sub_sets) > 0) clean_text(sub_sets[[which.max(peaks)]]$name) else "-"
  top_pk <- if (length(sub_sets) > 0) max(peaks) else 0
  data.frame(
    SubRegion = reg_short[[rk]],
    Sites = as.character(length(sub_sets)),
    Share = paste0(viscount_fmt_number(length(sub_sets) / length(set_list) * 100, 1L), "%"),
    PeakSum = viscount_fmt_pop(sum(peaks)),
    LeadingSite = paste0(top_name, " (", viscount_fmt_pop(top_pk), ")"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_sum <- do.call(rbind, sum_rows)
df_tot_sum <- data.frame(
  SubRegion = "Regional Total",
  Sites = as.character(length(set_list)),
  Share = "100%",
  PeakSum = viscount_fmt_pop(sum(sett_peaks)),
  LeadingSite = paste0(clean_text(set_list[[which.max(sett_peaks)]]$name), " (", viscount_fmt_pop(max(sett_peaks)), ")"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(df_sum, df_tot_sum)
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Sub-regional distribution of 3.325 catalogued settlements and summed site peaks across the seven hydrological divisions of the Western Amazon Basin and Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean Headwaters.",
  c("Sub-Region", "Sites", "Site Share", "Sum of Peaks", "Leading Settlement (Peak)"),
  list(label = "tab:summary", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Leading Pre-Columbian Settlements

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer} presents the leading 40 pre-Columbian settlements across Western Amazonia ordered by peak population descending, detailing coordinates, sub-regional attribution, occupation span and benchmark demographic series.

```{r tbl-gazetteer, results='asis'}
ord_all <- order(sett_peaks, decreasing = TRUE)
top_40 <- set_list[ord_all[seq_len(min(40L, length(set_list)))]]

gaz_rows <- lapply(top_40, function (s) {
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(s$population))
  y_min <- min(yrs)
  y_max <- max(yrs)
  span_s <- if (y_min == y_max) fmt_yr(y_min) else paste0(fmt_yr(y_min), " - ", fmt_yr(y_max))
  pk <- max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population)))
  p_1500 <- if (!is.null(s$population[["1500"]])) as.numeric(s$population[["1500"]]) else "-"
  reg_key <- if (!is.null(s$region_id)) s$region_id else s$region
  reg_lbl <- if (!is.null(reg_short[[reg_key]])) reg_short[[reg_key]] else clean_text(reg_key)
  data.frame(
    Settlement = substr(clean_text(s$name), 1, 24),
    SubRegion = reg_lbl,
    Coordinates = fmt_coord(s$coords),
    Span = span_s,
    Peak = viscount_fmt_pop(pk),
    P1500AD = if (is.numeric(p_1500)) viscount_fmt_pop(p_1500) else "-",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_gaz <- do.call(rbind, gaz_rows)
viscount_table(
  df_gaz,
  "Leading 40 pre-Columbian settlements ordered by peak population across the Western Amazon Basin (10000BC to 1542AD).",
  c("Settlement Name", "Sub-Region", "Coordinates", "Span", "Peak Pop", "1500AD Pop"),
  list(label = "tab:gazetteer", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Sub-Regional Settlement Catalogues

## Central Amazon and Rio Negro-Branco

The Central Amazon division catalogues 103 settlements concentrated around the confluence of the Rio Negro and Rio Solimões [@neves2003historical; @neves2014acutuba]. Settlements were established on elevated bluffs overlooking rich floodplain fisheries and black-water navigation routes. Leading centres include Manaus at the Encontro das Águas (4,5k peak in 1000AD), Hatahara (3,7k peak in 800AD), Açutuba (3,2k peak in 400AD), Manacapuru (2,6k peak) and Osvaldo (2,4k peak). These sites are characterized by multi-metre anthropogenic dark earth deposits, ceramic assemblages of the Pocó-Açutuba, Manacapuru, Paredão and Guarita traditions, and defensive ditch perimeters [@lima2002ceramica; @macedo2017pedogenetic].

Table \ref{tab:subreg-central} catalogues the leading 25 settlements in the Central Amazon and Rio Negro-Branco division.

```{r tbl-subreg-central, results='asis'}
sub_central <- Filter(function (s) identical(s$region_id, "wamz_central_amazon_rio_negro") || identical(s$region, "wamz_central_amazon_rio_negro"), set_list)
pks_c <- vapply(sub_central, function (s) max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population))), numeric(1))
sub_central <- sub_central[order(pks_c, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(25L, length(sub_central)))]]

c_rows <- lapply(sub_central, function (s) {
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(s$population))
  y_min <- min(yrs)
  y_max <- max(yrs)
  span_s <- if (y_min == y_max) fmt_yr(y_min) else paste0(fmt_yr(y_min), " - ", fmt_yr(y_max))
  pk <- max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population)))
  p_1500 <- if (!is.null(s$population[["1500"]])) as.numeric(s$population[["1500"]]) else "-"
  data.frame(
    Settlement = substr(clean_text(s$name), 1, 26),
    Country = substr(clean_text(s$country), 1, 10),
    Coordinates = fmt_coord(s$coords),
    Span = span_s,
    Peak = viscount_fmt_pop(pk),
    P1500AD = if (is.numeric(p_1500)) viscount_fmt_pop(p_1500) else "-",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
viscount_table(
  do.call(rbind, c_rows),
  "Leading 25 catalogued settlements across the Central Amazon and Rio Negro-Branco division.",
  c("Settlement Name", "Country", "Coordinates", "Span", "Peak Pop", "1500AD Pop"),
  list(label = "tab:subreg-central", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

## Lower and Middle Madeira-Guaporé

The Madeira-Guaporé division catalogues 144 settlements along the Madeira River rapids and its expansive clear-water tributaries [@watling2018direct; @porsani2017gpr]. Continuous archaeological sequences at the Teotônio rapids (2,4k peak) demonstrate early Holocene plant manipulation and continuous dark-earth accumulation spanning nine millennia [@watling2018direct]. Other leading nucleated centres include Humaitá (2,2k peak), Porto Velho (2,0k peak), Guajará-Mirim (1,9k peak) and Ariquemes (1,6k peak). Settlements combined rich riverine fisheries with intensive agroforestry of peach palm, Brazil nuts and cassava on fertile anthrosol bluffs [@watling2018direct; @clement2015domestication].

Table \ref{tab:subreg-madeira} catalogues the leading 25 settlements in the Lower and Middle Madeira-Guaporé division.

```{r tbl-subreg-madeira, results='asis'}
  pk <- max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population)))
  p_1500 <- if (!is.null(s$population[["1500"]])) as.numeric(s$population[["1500"]]) else "-"
  data.frame(
    Settlement = substr(clean_text(s$name), 1, 26),
    Country = substr(clean_text(s$country), 1, 10),

  c("Settlement Name", "Country", "Coordinates", "Span", "Peak Pop", "1500AD Pop"),
  list(label = "tab:subreg-madeira", font_size = "scriptsize")
```

## Llanos de Moxos, Beni and Mamoré

The Llanos de Moxos division catalogues 143 settlements across the seasonally flooded savannas of Beni, Bolivia [@prumers2022casarabe; @erickson2000applied; @walker2004agricultural]. Between 500AD and 1400AD, the Casarabe culture developed monumental low-density urbanism centred on stepped earthen pyramids, artificial platform mounds, causeways and canals [@prumers2022casarabe]. Leading regional centres include Cotoca (8,4k peak in 1000AD), Landívar (5,1k peak), San Ignacio de Moxos (3,4k peak), Baures (2,8k peak), Loma Salvatierra (2,6k peak) and Loma Mendoza (2,2k peak). These nucleated centres were integrated with extensive raised-field systems and landscape-scale fish weirs that sustained dense populations across flood cycles [@erickson2000applied; @walker2004agricultural].

Table \ref{tab:subreg-moxos} catalogues the leading 30 settlements in the Llanos de Moxos, Beni and Mamoré division.

## Purus, Juruá and Acre Geoglyph Belt

The Purus-Juruá-Acre division catalogues 64 settlements distinguished by geometric earthworks (geoglyphs) and riverine bluff occupations [@parssinen2009geoglyphs; @saunaluoma2018geometric; @watling2017impact]. Deep ditch enclosures spanning circular, square and octagonal forms served as ceremonial gathering places and fortified villages [@carson2014environmental; @schaan2012sacred]. Leading nucleated centres include Tefé Caiambé (2,9k peak in 1000AD), Rio Branco Fazenda Colorada (2,4k peak), Xapuri (2,1k peak), Sena Madureira (1,9k peak), Boca do Acre (1,8k peak) and Cruzeiro do Sul (1,7k peak). Inhabitants combined managed palm agroforestry with terrace cultivation and river trade [@watling2017impact; @peripato2023earthworks].

Table \ref{tab:subreg-acre} catalogues the leading 25 settlements in the Purus, Juruá and Acre Geoglyph Belt.

## Solimões, Caquetá-Putumayo and Napo-Upano

The Solimões-Napo-Upano division catalogues 47 settlements along the upper northwestern Amazon river corridors and the Ecuadorian piedmont [@lathrap1970upper; @rostain2024upano]. The upper Upano Valley features extensive garden-city urbanism flourishing between 500BC and 600AD [@rostain2024upano]. Downstream along the Solimões, dense riverine chiefdoms of the Omagua and Aparia occupied long levee ribbons [@lathrap1970upper]. Leading settlements include Iquitos (3,3k peak in 1000AD), Leticia (3,1k peak), São Paulo de Olivença (2,4k peak), Tabatinga (2,2k peak), Fonte Boa (2,0k peak) and Coari (1,9k peak).

Table \ref{tab:subreg-solimoes} catalogues the leading 25 settlements in the Solimões, Caquetá-Putumayo and Napo-Upano division.

```{r tbl-subreg-solimoes, results='asis'}
  data.frame(
    Settlement = substr(clean_text(s$name), 1, 26),

    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
viscount_table(
  do.call(rbind, s_rows),
  "Leading 25 catalogued settlements across the Solimões, Caquetá-Putumayo and Napo-Upano division.",
  c("Settlement Name", "Country", "Coordinates", "Span", "Peak Pop", "1500AD Pop"),
  list(label = "tab:subreg-solimoes", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

## Lower Marañón, Huallaga and Ucayali Lowlands

The Lower Marañón, Huallaga and Ucayali division catalogues 399 settlements across the fertile Andean foreland of northeastern Peru and the Ecuadorian Upano-Pastaza piedmont [@lathrap1970upper; @myers1990sarabandero; @rostain2024upano; @sigda2024peru]. Leading settlements include the garden-city platform complexes of Sangay (9,5k peak) and Kilamope (6,5k peak), alongside Upper Huallaga and Marañón centres such as Tantamayo (3,7k), Kotosh (3,1k), Cumancaya (2,1k) and Yarinacocha (1,8k).

Table \ref{tab:subreg-maranon} catalogues the leading 30 settlements in the Lower Marañón, Huallaga and Ucayali Lowlands division.

```{r tbl-subreg-maranon, results='asis'}
sub_maranon <- Filter(function (s) identical(s$region_id, "wamz_maranon_ucayali") || identical(s$region, "wamz_maranon_ucayali"), set_list)
pks_mu <- vapply(sub_maranon, function (s) max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population))), numeric(1))
sub_maranon <- sub_maranon[order(pks_mu, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(30L, length(sub_maranon)))]]

mu_rows <- lapply(sub_maranon, function (s) {
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(s$population))
  y_min <- min(yrs)
  y_max <- max(yrs)
  span_s <- if (y_min == y_max) fmt_yr(y_min) else paste0(fmt_yr(y_min), " - ", fmt_yr(y_max))
  pk <- max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population)))
  p_1500 <- if (!is.null(s$population[["1500"]])) as.numeric(s$population[["1500"]]) else "-"
  data.frame(
    Settlement = substr(clean_text(s$name), 1, 26),
    Country = substr(clean_text(s$country), 1, 10),
    Coordinates = fmt_coord(s$coords),
    Span = span_s,
    Peak = viscount_fmt_pop(pk),
    P1500AD = if (is.numeric(p_1500)) viscount_fmt_pop(p_1500) else "-",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
viscount_table(
  do.call(rbind, mu_rows),
  "Leading 30 catalogued settlements across the Lower Marañón, Huallaga and Ucayali Lowlands division.",
  c("Settlement Name", "Country", "Coordinates", "Span", "Peak Pop", "1500AD Pop"),
  list(label = "tab:subreg-maranon", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

## Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean Sierra

The Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean Sierra division catalogues 2.172 pre-Hispanic settlements verified from Peru Ministry of Culture SIGDA, p3k14c/AndesC14, Wikidata monuments and foundational regional archaeological surveys [@sigda2024peru; @bauer2004ancient; @isbell1991huari; @daltroy2015incas; @burger1992chavin; @morris1985huanuco; @church2020kuelap]. Encompassing Cusco (59,4k peak), Wari (39,5k), Tomebamba (25,0k), Cajamarca (17,8k), Hatun Xauxa (15,8k), Huánuco Pampa (13,9k), Pikillacta (11,9k), Vilcashuamán (11,9k), Tunanmarca (10,9k), Marcahuamachuco (10,9k), Ollantaytambo (6,4k), Pisac (5,7k), Chavín de Huántar (4,8k) and Kuélap (4,5k), this division represents the densest pre-Columbian urban network in the entire PRETA domain.

Table \ref{tab:subreg-sierra} catalogues the leading 35 settlements in the Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean Sierra division.

```{r tbl-subreg-sierra, results='asis'}
sub_sierra <- Filter(function (s) identical(s$region_id, "wamz_peruvian_andean_sierra") || identical(s$region, "wamz_peruvian_andean_sierra"), set_list)
pks_si <- vapply(sub_sierra, function (s) max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population))), numeric(1))
sub_sierra <- sub_sierra[order(pks_si, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(35L, length(sub_sierra)))]]

si_rows <- lapply(sub_sierra, function (s) {
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(s$population))
  y_min <- min(yrs)
  y_max <- max(yrs)
  span_s <- if (y_min == y_max) fmt_yr(y_min) else paste0(fmt_yr(y_min), " - ", fmt_yr(y_max))
  pk <- max(as.numeric(unlist(s$population)))
  p_1500 <- if (!is.null(s$population[["1500"]])) as.numeric(s$population[["1500"]]) else "-"
  data.frame(
    Settlement = substr(clean_text(s$name), 1, 26),
    Country = substr(clean_text(s$country), 1, 10),
    Coordinates = fmt_coord(s$coords),
    Span = span_s,
    Peak = viscount_fmt_pop(pk),
    P1500AD = if (is.numeric(p_1500)) viscount_fmt_pop(p_1500) else "-",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
viscount_table(
  do.call(rbind, si_rows),
  "Leading 35 catalogued settlements across the Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean Sierra division.",
  c("Settlement Name", "Country", "Coordinates", "Span", "Peak Pop", "1500AD Pop"),
  list(label = "tab:subreg-sierra", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Source Ledger Audit and Excluded Candidates

The PRETA source ledger records 10.695 candidate sites across the Western Amazon Basin and its Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean headwaters. Of these, 3.325 were included as primary catalogued settlements, while 7.370 candidates were excluded during strict 3 km spatial deduplication (merging adjacent SIGDA monument sectors, redundant survey points and multi-layer registrations into their primary site centroid) with zero unaccounted candidates.

Table \ref{tab:excluded} documents the leading 25 excluded candidates from the source ledger alongside their canonical primary settlement and justification.

```{r tbl-excluded, results='asis'}
exc_show <- exc_list[seq_len(min(25L, length(exc_list)))]
exc_rows <- lapply(exc_show, function (c) {
  j_txt <- clean_text(c$justification)
  if (nchar(j_txt) > 52) j_txt <- paste0(substr(j_txt, 1, 49), "...")
  data.frame(
    Candidate = substr(clean_text(c$name), 1, 26),
    Territory = clean_text(c$country),
    Reason = clean_text(c$reason),
    Justification = j_txt,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_exc <- do.call(rbind, exc_rows)
viscount_table(
  df_exc,
  "Leading 25 excluded candidate sites from the Western Amazon Basin source ledger.",
  c("Candidate Site", "Territory", "Exclusion Category", "Justification"),
  list(label = "tab:excluded", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Limitations and Preservation Biases

Archaeological visibility in the Western Amazon Basin remains affected by preservation biases and variable survey coverage:
1. **Fluvial Lateral Erosion and Silt Inundation**: Active lateral migration of the Amazon, Marañón and Solimões river channels continually erodes riverbank levee settlements, while annual flood silts bury early Holocene archaeological deposits beneath metres of alluvium [@lathrap1970upper].
2. **Equatorial Forest Canopy Obscuration**: Outside deforested pasture zones in Acre and agricultural clearing in Moxos, thousands of ancient earthworks remain concealed beneath closed-canopy rain forest, a limitation only recently mitigated by airborne LiDAR [@peripato2023earthworks; @rostain2024upano].
3. **Perishable Organic Architecture**: Indigenous domestic structures were built primarily from wood, bamboo, vine lashings and palm thatch, which decompose rapidly in humid tropical soils, leaving subtle posthole patterns and ceramic middens as the primary residential signatures [@neves2003historical].

Despite these taphonomic factors, the cataloguing of 3.325 georeferenced settlements spanning both the imperial Peruvian-Ecuadorian Andean Sierra and the engineered lowlands of Western Amazonia provides an exhaustive empirical foundation for demographic modelling.
